Crocs Has a Trick for Dodging Taxes: A Tiny Office in Malta
Big American companies are shifting billions of dollars in profits to offices with few or zero employees, all in order to dodge income taxes. A prime example? The shoemaker Crocs.
Crocs claims that 100 percent of its profits were earned by a two-person office in an old brewery in Malta, a tiny archipelago that has become a hot tax haven.
In recent years, regulators have tried to crack down on these offshore maneuvers. But the E.U. has let some members, like Malta, delay a minimum corporate tax adopted by over 100 countries.
And, earlier this year, the Trump administration pulled the U.S. out of the effort, exempting American firms from most of the provisions and allowing them to shift profits abroad more easily.
